title: optimize quant kernels: int8/fp8 smoothquant + dequant fusion + kvcache/batching
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce CPU/GPU token cost for quantized models (INT8 and FP8 paths) by adding fused dequantization paths, improving SmoothQuant handling, and making kernel scheduling aware of kv-cache and continuous-batching patterns. This PR targets the hot inner loops used by decoder-only and encoder-decoder inference in the runtime, with the goal of improving per-token throughput and reducing tail latency for small-batch streaming workloads. What this change does: - Add fused dequantization + GEMM kernels for common INT8/FP8->FP16 execution paths (AVX512 and CUDA kernels where applicable). - Implement SmoothQuant-aware scaling propagation so we avoid unnecessary dequant/requant around attention blocks. - Introduce a dequant-fusion codepath that skips separate dequant + matmul calls when input is cached (kvcache case). - Make the scheduler aware of continuous-batching patterns so it prefers fused paths when streams are long-lived and KV cache hits are likely. - Add heuristics to prefer INT8-fused kernels for short-sequence low-latency requests and FP8 mixed paths for throughput-heavy scenarios. - Add targeted microbenchmarks and regression tests to the perf harness. Benchmarks (internal perf lab, rtx-a100-80gb, model: redwood-7b-quant): - Baseline (previous release): 1.0x throughput, p95 latency 210ms (single-stream, 1-token steps) - This PR (INT8 fused): 1.34x throughput, p95 latency 160ms - This PR (FP8 mixed + smoothquant): 1.22x throughput, p95 latency 170ms - End-to-end cost reduction estimate: ~25% token-cost reduction for mixed workloads. Numbers include kvcache warm start scenarios used by chat-style workloads. Compatibility: existing public API unchanged. The runtime selects the fused paths at runtime; no model-side changes required. Added feature gates to enable/disable the new kernels at runtime for canary rollouts. Files changed (high-level): runtime/quant/kernels/*.cpp/h — new fused kernels and CPU AVX512 path; runtime/quant/cuda_kernels.cu — optional CUDA fused kernels; runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.cpp — scheduling heuristics; runtime/kvcache/cache_optimizations.cpp — fast-path for cached-dequant; tests/perf/quant_benchmarks.py — microbench harness; tests/integration/quant_inference_ci.sh — CI smoke. Checklist: [x] unit tests added/updated for fused kernels [x] perf benchmarks added to benchmark-lab harness [x] feature flag to toggle fused paths [x] release notes entry included [x] canary rollout plan documented in PR description Rollout plan: enable feature flag in dedicated canary region (us-west-2) for 10% of traffic, monitor p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and model quality metrics (log-likelihood and a small prompt eval). If regressions found, flip flag off and revert for the canary. Full rollout after 1 week of stability and no quality regressions. Security/Compliance: no user data changes, no new secrets. Perf data recorded in existing telemetry. Related: ENG-4421 (quant kernel roadmap), ENG-4310 (kvcache continuous-batching), SUP-987 (customer report re: quantized tail latency).
